description: The DEVELOPER-side environment variable contract (what YOUR integration reads). Credential VALUES never appear in any file — only variable NAMES. ZECK_TOKEN is always a Zeck transport credential, never a provider API key: provider connections are BYOK references held server-side by the platform. The platform-side (operator) variable contract is owned by deploy/manifests/variables.json (DEP-001/D-01) — cross-referenced, never duplicated. This file is validated against examples/lib/env.ts by tests/unit/developer-docs/machine-schemas.test.ts.

variables.name: ZECK_API_URL
variables.description: The base URL of the Zeck public API of the environment you integrate against (e.g. a sandbox deployment).

variables.name: ZECK_TOKEN
variables.description: The bearer credential for the Zeck TRANSPORT. Never a provider API key; never passed on a command line (shell history is a leak surface); never committed.

variables.name: ZECK_APPLICATION_ID
variables.description: The application whose scope authorizes scoped reads and governed commands (sent as the X-Zeck-Application header by the SDK client's applicationId option).

variables.name: ZECK_ENVIRONMENT_ID
variables.description: Optional environment selector (e.g. a disposable sandbox environment) passed as environmentId on execution creation.

variables.name: ZECK_WEBHOOK_SECRET
variables.description: The webhook endpoint's signing secret for RECEIVER-side signature verification (arrives out-of-band; never in a URL, never logged).

variables.name: ZECK_WEBHOOK_PORT
variables.description: Local listen port of the webhook receiver example (default 9090).

providerCredentialNames.description: Credential env var NAMES the platform's authorized provider set reads SERVER-SIDE (never in your integration code; recorded availability lives in docs/developer/AVAILABILITY.md and docs/VALIDATION-REPORT.md). Listing a NAME here never implies the credential is present in any environment.
